entries.note: An exercise to either build or warm-up front and back neck muscles. Stand or sit with your head in neutral position. Place both of your hands on your forehead. entries.note: Sit on the bench with your toes pointing straight out, back straight and abs drawn in. Grip the bar with your palms facing outwards and your hands shoulder width apart. entries.name: Cable Front Raise
poses: Redraw the selected source pose for Cable Front Raise, source frame 2, with correct anatomy and equipment. One clear representative still only.
entries.note: Place the pulley on the setting just above the floor. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, your abs drawn in and your knees slightly bent. Starting at waist height, take the pulley in your left hand, palm facing the floor with otherwise known as an overhand grip, and raise your straight arm up towards your left shoulder. At shoulder height pause for a moment. With a controlled movement resist the weight and slowly lower your arm back to starting position at your waist. Repeat the exercise with your right arm. Maintain a good posture at all times during this exercise ensuring not swaying or arching at your back. Do not perform this exercise if you have shoulder pain.

entries.note: Grasp the handle of the low pulley with your right hand. Bend forward from the waist; your upper body should be nearly parallel with the floor. entries.name: Flat Bench Leg Raise
poses: Redraw the selected source pose for Flat Bench Leg Raise, source frame 2, with correct anatomy and equipment. One clear representative still only.
entries.note: Lie on a flat bench with your hands under your hips supporting your back. Your legs should be unsupported by the bench from below your knees. With your feet together and your toes flexed upwards, raise your straight legs up a few cm off the bench; both of your legs should have no contact with the bench. This is your starting position. Practice the squat without any weight to allow yourself to become comfortable with the movements. Do not sit on the bench during the exercise.

entries.note: Attach a belt with a weight plate or hold a dumbbell between your feet, then grip the bar shoulder-width apart with palms facing you and arms fully straight. Brace your core and pull your shoulders down away from your ears. Pull your chest toward the bar, driving your elbows down and back. Raise until your chin clears the bar. Lower yourself slowly until your arms are fully straight. Let the weight settle before you begin the next rep. Chest to the bar Full hang each rep No swinging

entries.name: Weighted Crunch
poses: Redraw the selected source pose for Weighted Crunch, source frame 1, with correct anatomy and equipment. One clear representative still only.
entries.note: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a plate against your chest. Brace your core and keep your lower back pressed down. Curl your ribs toward your hips, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abs. Lower slowly until your shoulders touch the floor. Keep the plate held close to your chest throughout. Ribs to hips Short range, strong squeeze Slow lowering

entries.name: Weighted Push-up
poses: Redraw the selected source pose for Weighted Push-up, source frame 1, with correct anatomy and equipment. One clear representative still only.
entries.note: Start in a push-up position with hands just wider than your shoulders, a weight plate or loaded pack secured on your upper back, and your body in one straight line. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock your body into a plank. Lower your chest to just above the floor with elbows about 45 degrees from your sides. Keep your neck neutral and your gaze a little ahead of your hands. Press the floor away until your arms are straight. Pause briefly at the top, then repeat for all reps without letting the load shift. Plank body, no sagging Elbows at 45 degrees Push the floor away

entries.name: World's Greatest Stretch

entries.note: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders. Step your right foot outside your right hand into a deep lunge. Lower your inner forearm toward the floor or a comfortable height. Rotate your chest toward the right and reach your right arm to the ceiling.
